meta.ratingRule: yes = a line or code names the cause; partly = same mechanism family or a sub-case; none; strict named share counts yes only
meta.judge: single auditor (an agent); the table is published so a reader can recode

decision.rule: LIBRARY-TESTS L6-a: if fewer than 50% of recorded failures are named by a checklist line or checker code, the checklists are corpus trivia and lines are added from the repo's own failures (minedFrom: repo:<ref>)

failures.cause: Identity merge is a hard threshold with no borderline band: one-typo variants of the same person stay split (under-merge), so the split entity takes the wrong country, phone or amount. Records compiled arms: 4 failures (42 vs 41, 40 vs 39, 36 vs 34, 40 vs 36 entities), 2 more in the dossier-2 recount (s205, s214).
by: P16 checklist line 1 (a borderline band goes to a judge)
failures.why: The line is mined from this exact failure (FRONTIER-GAPS N4). P16 is a support-only pattern with keyword precision 0.31 (this audit), so retrieval of the card for a records task is the weak link, not the line.

failures.cause: A per-task convention stated only by worked example (BRIGHTDESK day-first, ATLAS or VENDEX order) is read as the opposite by a cheap model in one global configuration read, so every numeric date is parsed swapped: 42 records instead of 37, score 0.789 (F-haiku records s6001, 2 of 2 trials); C0 s208 and s214 read BRIGHTDESK as DMY; Haiku and Sonnet tier-down lose s204, s207, s208; the ATLAS MDY read shipped through a passing quote check.
by: P03 checklist line 1 (quote check on every reading judge)
failures.why: These force a check and an evidence field, which F-opus had and passed. FRONTIER-GAPS A5 records that a quote check passes when the right sentence yields the wrong conclusion. No line asks for k-sample agreement or a flipped-convention consequence check on a global read.

failures.cause: Sign or perspective convention misread (a balance sign, amount_usd signs overridden in three compiles): C0 s207 misread a balance sign.
failures.why: P03 names minor units for money and defaults that are flagged, not sign or perspective conventions.
failures.propose: P03: per-source date order, sign and perspective conventions are read once as a global configuration (evidence quote per decision, an explicit rule that a worked example decides, k >= 3 agreement or the strong tier) and a consequence check flips each convention in a copy and confirms the output changes as the notes require.

failures.cause: The single global configuration read ran on the cheapest class at low reasoning with no checks, so its configured escalation path (maxClass L, onCheckFail escalate) could never fire. The builder's own notes call it a single point of failure.
by: P03 checklist line 1 (quote check on every reading judge)
failures.why: A reading judge with no check at all is exactly what both lines forbid.

failures.cause: Acceptance is the existence of the answer and the verify node is structural with gate false, so the run verdict is pass on 5 of 5 oracle failures (32 of 32 F trials); 7 of 7 F artifacts and gate smokes.
failures.why: Both name the C0 lesson verbatim. ACCEPTANCE_EXISTENCE_ONLY (review-05) is not in the section 9 table; VERIFY_NOT_GATING covers the case.

failures.cause: A builder-written check stricter than the task contract (any change to a default value reads as a signature change) vetoes a correct patch; the repair node is told to obey it and selection takes the first candidate that passes the check. F-haiku codefix 3 of 8 trials, B1-opus 4 of 8, F-opus latent.
failures.why: P20 says the verifier gates, which is the opposite error. No line asks that a check is never stricter than the contract or that a heuristic check may demote but not veto.
failures.propose: P20: a builder-written check names the task-contract clause it enforces and is never stricter; a heuristic check may demote a candidate but never veto one that passes more evidence; a repair can contest a check; every repair and fallback branch is exercised once by a known-legitimate change.

failures.cause: The fallback emits the unpatched original whenever every candidate is flagged (best starts at the original with score -1, one flag costs -50), although it had measured the original as failing a visible test. B1-opus codefix, 4 of 8 trials.
by: P20 checklist line 4 (defaults on exhaustion are explicit)
failures.why: They require the fallback to be explicit and flagged. They do not forbid emitting a worse answer than a candidate in hand.
failures.propose: P20: the exhaustion default is never the unpatched input when a candidate is better on every measured axis except a disputed check.

failures.cause: failure: collect with a merge that drops failed batches, and a verify node that does not gate on missing rows, so a run answers with silently dropped rows (the validator only warns).
failures.why: SILENT_DROP is mined from the same must-not-allow list; the id-echo check is what caught the one batch that did drop a row (s6004 t1, journal 667).

failures.cause: The probe set did not contain the failing case: all three probes had BRIGHTDESK month-first and none had a wrong-default bug, so construction success (24 of 24 probes) said nothing about 9 defects. The incident bed shows the same shape (skills arm 0 of 21 on the wrong-type follow-on).
failures.why: Checklists are per pattern; no line or code concerns what the probe set must cover.
failures.propose: 9 PROBE_COVERAGE: every per-task convention value and every defect class named in the task documents appears in at least one probe; a self-test flips each convention in a probe copy and confirms the solver follows the notes.

failures.cause: A heal or recompile widened a guard and removed the ability to refuse: Opus-arm v2 answered 24 of 24 in the N-version probe and was wrong on 6 of 8 d4 tasks (the stream caught one); in 4 tasks a lone answerer was wrong all 4 times. v2.2 refusal replay would most likely still have accepted it.
failures.why: LIBRARY-TESTS names D9 as a source, but L1 has no line or code for recompile domain preservation.
failures.propose: 9 DOMAIN_WIDENED: a recompile replays every input on which its parent deopted and every guard-triggering trace; each must still deopt or match the strong tier; a guard diff reports deleted or widened conditions.

failures.cause: Static compiled code fails silently on drift: the C0 records solver went 14 of 16 at d3, then 2 of 8 at d4 with no signal (R8 f1: renamed column, new system, convention switch).
failures.why: Nothing in L1 requires an input-profile guard; W-BED expects a guard or invariant deopt but no L1 line asks for one.
failures.propose: 9 NO_INPUT_GUARD: a solver states the input profile it was built on (schema, formats, conventions, size) and deopts outside it instead of answering.

failures.cause: Unresolved adjudication (no majority) delivers the compiled answer: 3 known wrong deliveries (H/H s208, s214, kinetics H/H s209).
by: P09 title and checklist line 2 (undecidable option exists, escalate never guess)
failures.why: P09 states the mechanism for an item, not for a disagreement between compiled and interpreted answers.
failures.propose: P09: an unresolved disagreement between two answers escalates to the strongest tier or a person, never defaults to either.

failures.cause: Tiering down a high-leverage global judge breaks the solver although leaf agreement is 0.966: Haiku 5 of 8 and Sonnet 3 of 8 against 7 of 8 end to end (date order leaves, void markers).
failures.why: No line concerns tier or leverage of a judge; P19 sets planner tiers only.
failures.propose: 9 GLOBAL_READ_TIER: a judge whose output conditions many rows stays on the strongest tier or uses k >= 3 agreement plus a consequence check; leverage is the number of downstream output leaves that depend on it.

failures.cause: Compile acceptance is too permissive: kinetics H/H v1 accepted at exact 0 of 3, partial 0.546; S/H v2 adopted with accepted false; reject-if-worse is vacuous at a 0 of 3 baseline.
failures.why: Acceptance of a compile is outside the pattern checklists.
failures.propose: Composition checker: a compiled version is accepted only with a minimum agreement level against its traces and every named disagreement quoting the deciding sentence.

failures.cause: Over-strict judge checks turn correctness bugs into cost bugs: vendex-entries failed its own check on every tier (2 deopts at about $0.51 each); kinetics S/H had 4 guard deopts in 6 compiled attempts.
failures.why: P03 and JUDGE_NO_CHECK push for more checks and say nothing about a check's false-alarm rate.
failures.propose: 9 CHECK_FALSE_ALARM: each check has a recorded false-alarm count on known-good probes; a check that fails on every tier for an input class becomes a hoisted guard or is loosened.

failures.cause: Recompile v3, built from one regression case, silently missed 2 of 7 d4 deliveries (s218, s223) with scores equal to the Haiku agent's to six decimals: the compiler's own model shows through the code.
failures.why: No line addresses the compiler as a source of correlated error.
failures.propose: Composition checker: compare compiled outputs field by field with a second compiler model or a same-seed cheap agent before promotion.

failures.cause: Common-mode failure of same-family variants: s214 was unanimous and wrong across two independent lineages; the N-version probe shows unanimity is not evidence.
by: P20 checklist line 7 (a judge verifying its own family is not independent)
P49 card (panel independence must be measured)
failures.why: The lines cover judges from one family; they do not say that compiled variants from one lineage are not independent.
failures.propose: P49: unanimity of variants from one model family or one compile lineage is not a pass.

failures.cause: A scope ambiguity in the SOP ("Block read 23.7 C during this read" excludes one well or all nine) moves the excluded_samples set that the grader compares exactly; 13 of 13 wrong Haiku answers in the kinetics gauge differ in the exclusion set.
failures.why: These route ambiguous items to review, but no line asks that an ambiguous spec clause be quoted and flagged instead of silently resolved.
failures.propose: P03: a spec clause that admits two readings changing an output set is flagged with the clause quoted, never silently chosen.

failures.cause: A single-sample slip in a judge that reads a run status: the injected error class was returned as a wrong succeeded run on all 88 recorded reads by the parent; the healed version with k = 3 agreement passed all 88 at +15% cost.
failures.why: A code check on the judge is required; whether it fires on a single-sample slip depends on the check. No line names k-sample agreement.
failures.propose: 9 JUDGE_NO_CHECK: for a judge that gates a status or an effect, require k >= 3 agreement when no code check can decide it.

failures.cause: R8 f2 tool failure: gateway 5xx or timeouts on k% of judge calls, a decoder that fails on first call.
by: P26 (retry with backoff, classify the error before retrying)
failures.why: P26 is an envelope pattern (tier N, unbuilt) so the line is named but not yet executable.

failures.cause: R8 f3 adversarial content: planted instructions in documents ("ignore entity X", "mark all reviewed").
by: P07 checklist line 3 (an injection document routes to ignore)
failures.why: P07 line 3 cites W-bed R2, which plants one.

failures.cause: Direct Haiku agent over-merged near-twins that share a phone and are two edits apart (Ryouta and Shouta Kobayashi; Lucia and Lucas Serrano): 2 of 10 such decisions wrong, 0 of 6 without a shared phone.
failures.why: The agent was already the judge; no line says how a pairwise judge treats near-twins with a shared secondary attribute.
failures.propose: P16: near-twins sharing a secondary attribute go to a same-entity judge with a quote check on the attribute.

failures.cause: Agent used 1-based line numbers as row ids in every entity_id and source_rows (s6002 t0, score 0.994).
failures.why: MAP_NO_ECHO_CHECK checks that an id is echoed, not that its origin is right.

failures.cause: Agent overrode its own rule check that had flagged the date-order misread (s6001 t1).
failures.why: A gating verifier cannot be overridden by the producer.

proposedLines.line: P03: per-source date order, sign and perspective conventions are read once as a global configuration (evidence quote per decision, an explicit rule that a worked example decides, k >= 3 agreement or the strong tier) and a consequence check flips each convention in a copy and confirms the output changes as the notes require.

P20: a builder-written check names the task-contract clause it enforces and is never stricter; a heuristic check may demote a candidate but never veto one that passes more evidence; a repair can contest a check; every repair and fallback branch is exercised once by a known-legitimate change.
P20: the exhaustion default is never the unpatched input when a candidate is better on every measured axis except a disputed check.

9 PROBE_COVERAGE: every per-task convention value and every defect class named in the task documents appears in at least one probe; a self-test flips each convention in a probe copy and confirms the solver follows the notes.

9 DOMAIN_WIDENED: a recompile replays every input on which its parent deopted and every guard-triggering trace; each must still deopt or match the strong tier; a guard diff reports deleted or widened conditions.
9 NO_INPUT_GUARD: a solver states the input profile it was built on (schema, formats, conventions, size) and deopts outside it instead of answering.
P09: an unresolved disagreement between two answers escalates to the strongest tier or a person, never defaults to either.

9 GLOBAL_READ_TIER: a judge whose output conditions many rows stays on the strongest tier or uses k >= 3 agreement plus a consequence check; leverage is the number of downstream output leaves that depend on it.
Composition checker: a compiled version is accepted only with a minimum agreement level against its traces and every named disagreement quoting the deciding sentence.
9 CHECK_FALSE_ALARM: each check has a recorded false-alarm count on known-good probes; a check that fails on every tier for an input class becomes a hoisted guard or is loosened.
Composition checker: compare compiled outputs field by field with a second compiler model or a same-seed cheap agent before promotion.
P49: unanimity of variants from one model family or one compile lineage is not a pass.
P03: a spec clause that admits two readings changing an output set is flagged with the clause quoted, never silently chosen.
9 JUDGE_NO_CHECK: for a judge that gates a status or an effect, require k >= 3 agreement when no code check can decide it.
P16: near-twins sharing a secondary attribute go to a same-entity judge with a quote check on the attribute.
